title: Hermes and Nerve Foundations
summary: What Hermes is, what Nerve adds, and where authority lives

lessons.title: What Hermes owns
lessons.body: Hermes is the agent runtime: model providers, tools, sessions, approvals, and the Kanban board are Hermes-owned surfaces. Nerve never replaces them; it observes and advises.

lessons.title: What Nerve adds
lessons.body: Nerve is a supervisory nervous system: risk-aware HITL gating, verified experience, selective context, Reflex providers, work supervision, profiles, a control panel, and the university.

lessons.title: Authority rules
lessons.body: Canonical truth (task state, completion, config) always lives in Hermes. Nerve components may advise, gate, or annotate - they never overwrite Hermes authority.

lab.goal: Identify which surface owns each of: task completion, tool approval, provider selection, experience notes.
steps: Create a disposable sandbox: export HERMES_HOME=/tmp/uni-lab-1 && mkdir -p $HERMES_HOME
Run: hermes --version  (observe the install directory line)
List the sandbox: ls $HERMES_HOME  (note it is empty until Hermes initializes it)
lab.expect: You can name the owner surface for each item without opening the code.

task.intro: Answer the scenario questions; the engine verifies them deterministically in a disposable fixture. Your answers are never executed as commands.

questions.why: Hermes executes and owns canonical lifecycle; Nerve supervises.
The operator owns policy and consequential decisions.
Nerve advises and verifies but never bypasses Hermes security.

executable.task: Produce an ownership map assigning each surface to its rightful owner.

check.question: Q: Which component owns canonical task completion? (hermes/nerve/either)

troubleshooting: If a plugin claims to complete tasks directly, that is a Paperclip-style private integration, not core Nerve behavior.
Nerve's work module routes completion through Hermes' native dispatcher.
